page: Microsoft Azure E96-48s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz across 24 physical cores, yielding 48 dedicated virtual CPUs via two threads per core on the x86_64 architecture. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache pool. Architectural instruction capabilities include AVX-512 with VNNI, along with hardware-level cryptographic acceleration including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 672.0 GB of system memory, representing a dense 14.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware profile bundles zero local storage and no graphics accelerators, directing all persistent storage demands to external attached block volumes.

Empirical benchmark results demonstrate substantial memory subsystem throughput and capable vectorized computation. The instance delivers uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 263.69 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 128.61 GB/sec, placing it within the top 25 percent of tested systems. This memory performance is reinforced by a PassMark memory score of 2850.91 and strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance of 230.56 GB/sec. Compute benchmarks show strong cryptographic throughput, recording 43888.24 on the PassMark CPU encryption test, alongside a solid overall PassMark CPU score of 51120.63. Standard synthetic compute metrics fall into median percentiles, including stress-ng multi-core performance of 46618.31 and Geekbench multi-core performance of 15621.0.

The constrained vCPU configuration of the E96-48s_v5 enables organizations to maximize available memory capacity while curbing per-core software licensing expenditures. Because no ephemeral or high-speed local NVMe storage is bundled, all persistence relies on remote block storage, introducing network latency considerations for storage-bound pipelines. Supported by strong PassMark database operations scores (23498.42) and high static web serving throughput (48.04 GB/sec), this server is designed for high-capacity in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, heavy data extraction and transformation (ETL) routines, and memory-constrained enterprise applications.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-48s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor at 2.8 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it features AVX-512 VNNI, cryptographic extensions, and 48 MB of L3 cache. With 672.0 GB of total RAM, it delivers an elevated 14.0 GB of memory per vCPU, without bundled local disk storage or dedicated GPU acceleration. Benchmark testing confirms top-tier memory bandwidth, reaching 263.69 GB/sec in uncached read operations, strong encryption speeds, and top-quartile database operation indices. General processor benchmarks position the instance within expected mid-tier multi-core ranges. This core-constrained profile provides substantial memory capacity for memory-bound enterprise systems, in-memory caching solutions, and complex ETL pipelines reliant on external storage networks.
